result.title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
result.summary: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个分层统计框架，将 agent 评测划分为场景、实例、样本三层，为 mean pass rate、pass@k、passhat^k 给出不确定性估计与有限样本方差表达式，并把分层聚合与统计物理中的粗粒化对应起来，从而将执行噪声与任务异质性分离。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其方差分解可用于核查 latent 推理中采样随机性与任务难度的混淆、以及 STOP 决策可靠性的评测口径，可供参考。
